record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: For a signed graph Σ, determine the maximum number p′+(Σ) of pairwise edge-disjoint positive circles.

evidence.quote: Qn. 3+. Evaluate p′+(Σ), given Σ. Ans. Unknown.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph $\Sigma = (G, \sigma)$ consists of a finite graph $G = (V, E)$ together with a sign function $\sigma : E \to \{+1, -1\}$. A circle (cycle) of $\Sigma$ is a connected 2-regular subgraph; its sign is the product of the signs of its edges. A circle is called positive if its sign is $+1$.

Define
$$p'_+(\Sigma) := \max\bigl\{\, k : \Sigma \text{ contains } k \text{ pairwise edge-disjoint positive circles}\,\bigr\}.$$

Problem. Give a formula, characterization, or efficient method to evaluate $p'_+(\Sigma)$ for an arbitrary signed graph $\Sigma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of evaluating the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint positive circles in a signed graph appears in Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative and positive circles, where it is explicitly listed as having unknown answer. Recent works (e.g., on weakly negative circles versus best clustering, 2024) continue to address related packing/covering problems for signed graphs but do not announce a general solution to the edge-disjoint positive circle packing problem.
